motivation: FormatSource::capture copied TextFragments for every block of complete guarded list roots; both callers then discarded blocks outside the normalized selection. A one-item selection in a 500-item list unnecessarily materialized 500 fragments for each heading action evaluation.
change: Retain complete source root guards and original layout, but skip text capture for block paths strictly outside the normalized inclusive endpoint paths. Root/path enumeration remains intact. No changes to the registry, action-state cache, preflight, document limits, operation recipe, codecs, selection relocation, public API or default shipping behavior.
correctness: Both callers first require the sealed flat-list schema and normalize a selection from a validated immutable EditorState. They already discarded precisely these outside-range blocks before deriving indicators and operations. The helper still captures an empty endpoint and an end block at offset zero; the inline and block-kind callers retain their distinct endpoint policies. Complete root guards and layout, operation construction, full result validation and registry transaction preflight remain unchanged.
redGreenRegressions: Before the helper change, the large-list regression failed with 500 captured blocks versus one expected; mixed-root capture failed with five paths versus three expected. The focused command exited 101 with exactly these two assertion failures.

After the change, tests cover first/middle/last item and two-item ranges in both directions, exact complete ordered-list guards and 500-item layout, Unicode lengths, mixed bare/bullet/numbered roots, empty start block and a zero-offset end block.

All 1128 all-feature core library tests pass, including existing public registry/session tests for exact selection, pending formats, history, activation, disabled reasons, complete-result limits and V6 codec round trips.
verification: Private Wasm candidate passes strict generated TypeScript/declarations, 14 declaration tests, Node heading/list/recovery checks and five raw-Wasm runs per engine.
Private installed packages pass Node/type/base-consumer and flat-list smoke checks in Chromium, Firefox and WebKit.
Complete packaged browser matrix: 165 passed, zero skipped, unexpected or flaky results.
List demo matrix: 54 passed, zero skipped, unexpected or flaky results.
Six sequential unprofiled production performance runs: all 162 exact-state cases pass across three engines.
Shipping distribution hashes remain unchanged. Scoped sleep-prevention processes completed; pmset reports zero PreventSystemSleep and PreventUserIdleSystemSleep assertions.

performance.method: Sequential production-minified installed-package runs after build and regression processes completed. Three independent owners at each of 10/100/500 items per engine; exact selection, document, edit, undo, checkpoint, restore and redo assertions outside measured spans. Baseline/candidate, baseline/candidate, then reversed candidate/baseline. No profiler or diagnostic instrumentation. Apple M1 Pro, headless Chromium 151.0.7922.34, Firefox 153.0 and WebKit 26.5. Scoped sleep prevention; uncontrolled background host load. Per-run medians below are rounded to 0.1 ms, not statistical p95 or release performance qualification.
performance.decision: Retain this small capture-scope correction. Firefox 500-item edit medians improve by 4-7 ms (about 2-4%) in each pair, including reversed order. Firefox selection, undo, restore and redo also improve in each pair. Chromium edit results are mixed; WebKit is equal or lower but variable. Do not claim a general all-engine speedup. The exact capture-count regression proves removal of unnecessary text copies independently of noisy wall-clock timings. Large-list responsiveness remains unfinished.

remaining: Responsiveness, human native IME/VoiceOver checks, intermittent WebKit faults, delivery/size policy and full release qualification remain open. No version change, shipping rebuild, push or publish.
